title: Unified Traffic Routing for Polyglot Microservices
business: A global retail platform operating a polyglot architecture with services written in Java, Go, and Python.
problem: The engineering team struggles with inconsistent load balancing and observability across disparate service frameworks, leading to silent failures during inter-service communication.
solution: Deploy Envoy as a sidecar proxy alongside every application instance to provide a uniform L7 communication bus, standardizing routing, load balancing, and telemetry collection regardless of the underlying application language.
steps: Deploy an Envoy sidecar process alongside each application container to intercept all inbound and outbound traffic.
Configure the HTTP connection manager to handle L7 routing and protocol bridging between HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
Enable the outlier detection subsystem to perform passive health checking and automatically eject unhealthy upstream hosts.
Integrate the Envoy administration port with a centralized statistics sink to aggregate observability data across the entire mesh.
outcome: A transparent communication mesh where developers focus on application logic while Envoy ensures consistent traffic management and visibility.
limitation: The out-of-process architecture introduces a small latency overhead per hop; verify this by monitoring the Envoy-reported request duration statistics via the administration interface.

questions.question: In Unified Traffic Routing for Polyglot Microservices, what is the primary reason for using Envoy sidecars?
options: To replace the application logic with proxy logic
To standardize routing and observability across different languages
To eliminate the need for HTTP/2 support
To increase the complexity of the network topology
questions.explanation: Envoy provides a uniform communication bus that works across different languages, solving the problem of inconsistent management in polyglot environments.
questions.evidence: Deploy Envoy as a sidecar proxy alongside every application instance to provide a uniform L7 communication bus, standardizing routing, load balancing, and telemetry collection regardless of the underlying application language.

questions.question: In Unified Traffic Routing for Polyglot Microservices, what is a known limitation of the sidecar architecture?
options: It prevents the use of HTTP/2
It requires all services to be written in C++
It introduces a small latency overhead per hop
It cannot perform passive health checking
questions.explanation: Running an out-of-process proxy adds a network hop, which introduces a small amount of latency that must be monitored.
questions.evidence: The out-of-process architecture introduces a small latency overhead per hop; verify this by monitoring the Envoy-reported request duration statistics via the administration interface.
